canonical_name: The International Award for Young People (Duke of Edinburgh's International Award)
organizer: The International Award Foundation (global); operated in Türkiye by TİKAV (Türkiye İnsan Kaynağını Geliştirme Vakfı)
eligibility_verbatim: available to all 14 to 24-year-olds, inclusive of all backgrounds, locations, cultures and abilities (global site); Turkey operator: '14 - 24 yaş aralığında olmanız yeterlidir'. Level-specific minimum ages in Turkey: Bronze 14+, Silver 15+, Gold 16+.
eligible_grades: Roughly grades 9-12 and beyond (age-based, not grade-based)
turkey_access_reasoning: TİKAV (Türkiye İnsan Kaynağını Geliştirme Vakfı) is the officially licensed national operator for Türkiye, confirmed on both intaward.org (global) and intaward.org.tr (Turkey). Open to any student aged 14-24 via a participating school's Award Coordinator, or by independent/individual application by emailing bagimsiz@tikav.org.tr with no school-nomination gatekeeping required. No citizenship restriction found; open to Turkey residents generally.
international_access_notes: Operates in 120+ countries; the Bronze/Silver/Gold certificate is portable and internationally recognized, useful on applications to universities outside Türkiye as well as within it.
minimum_activity_duration: Bronze: minimum 6 months; Silver: minimum 12 months; Gold: minimum 18 months (across Volunteering, Skills, Physical, and Expedition sections; Gold adds a 5th Community Service Project section).
geographic_restrictions: None found beyond needing a licensed national operator (Türkiye has one via TİKAV); open to all youth in Türkiye regardless of background per official copy.
current_cycle_label: Rolling enrollment; not a fixed annual application cycle
cost_notes: Turkey operator confirms an annual 'Katılım Bağışı' (participation donation) is required before starting; exact current TL amount not stated on the pages fetched directly. A secondary (non-official) source cited approx. 150 TL -- not independently confirmed by us against an official price list, so left unset rather than guessed.
output_type: documented record of sustained extracurricular activity

evidence.raw_excerpt: a Non-Formal Education and Learning framework... available to all 14 to 24-year-olds, inclusive of all backgrounds, locations, cultures and abilities... over a million young people participating at any one time... founded in 1956.
Gençler, Ödül'e kendi okulları ve gençlik merkezleri aracılığıyla ya da bireysel olarak ulaşırlar.

14 - 24 yaş aralığında olmanız yeterlidir... Ödül Programı okulunuzda yürütülüyorsa... okulunuzdaki Ödül Koordinatörü'yle iletişime geçiniz... [veya email] bagimsiz@tikav.org.tr ... senelik olarak belirlenmiş 'Katılım Bağışı' tutarını ödeyerek.
Bronz: en az 6 aydır (14-24 yaş)... Gümüş: en az 12 aydır (15-24 yaş)... Altın: en az 18 aydır (16-24 yaş).

notes_uncertainties: Exact current participation fee amount in TL not confirmed directly from an official price page. Very well-established global program (est. 1956, 120+ countries) with a genuine, officially licensed Turkey operator (TİKAV) -- high confidence overall on eligibility and structure.

organizer: The Diana Award (UK-registered charity, established in memory of Diana, Princess of Wales)
eligibility_verbatim: Nominees must be between 16 and 24 years old at the time of nomination (may be 25 when receiving the award). Social action work must have been ongoing for a minimum of 12 months. Work must align with one of four SDG focus areas: Quality Education, Reduced Inequality, Good Health & Wellbeing, Climate Action.
eligible_grades: Roughly grades 11-12 and first years of university/gap year (age-based)
turkey_access_reasoning: Official page states: 'The Diana Award is a global honour. Since 2020, we've recognised young social activists in over 80 countries across six continents.' No citizenship or country restriction found. Condition: nomination-only (self-nomination not allowed) -- needs a nominator (age 18+, professional relationship) plus two professional supporters, a real access barrier for a student without an adult mentor/teacher/NGO contact willing to nominate them, but not a geographic barrier.
international_access_notes: Explicitly global; recognized activists on six continents. No evidence of a US/UK-only restriction.
minimum_activity_duration: Minimum 12 months of sustained social action work
geographic_restrictions: None found; explicitly global ('80 countries across six continents' since 2020).
cost_notes: No cost mentioned; nomination-based, free to nominee.
output_type: Publication on the Roll of Honour
access to global network of young leaders / Conversations for Change

evidence.raw_excerpt: Nominees must be between 16 and 24 years old at the time of nomination... a minimum of 12 months, demonstrating sustained impact, commitment, and sustainability... The Diana Award is a global honour. Since 2020, we've recognised young social activists in over 80 countries across six continents... Nominations for the 2026 Diana Award are now closed (deadline was 31 October 2025, 17:00 GMT)... Self-nominations are not allowed... Up to 200 exceptional young people receive the award annually.

notes_uncertainties: 2026 cycle nominations already closed (deadline was 31 Oct 2025); 2027 cycle deadline not yet published as of this research date -- recorded as null/next_cycle_not_published rather than guessed. No specific past Turkey recipients were confirmed or denied by the page; the general 'six continents' claim is the basis for ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS rather than VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE since the real gating condition is finding a qualified nominator, not geography.

aliases: The Explorers Club Rising Explorer Grant
eligibility_verbatim: Open to high school students and college undergraduates worldwide, and independent researchers doing work at an equivalent level. Project must be true science -- designed to generate new knowledge -- not an adventure, travel experience, or school field trip.
turkey_access_reasoning: Official page states the grant 'welcomes applications from students around the world regardless of nationality, ethnicity, or geographic location' and is open to high school students worldwide. No country restriction found.
international_access_notes: Explicitly worldwide; no travel to the US required to apply (fieldwork can be done anywhere, including Türkiye).
output_type: automatic consideration for Explorers Club membership

evidence.raw_excerpt: This program is open to high school students and college undergraduates worldwide... applicants from every background and every corner of the globe... Awards average $2,000... August 31, 2026, 6:00 PM ET... Successful applicants receive automatic consideration for Explorers Club membership.

notes_uncertainties: Deadline shown (2026-08-31) is very close to this research date (2026-08-26); this is the CURRENT open cycle, confirmed directly from the official grants page fetched today, not a stale prior-year date. Appears to be an annual/recurring grant based on program design, but the exact 2027 cycle timing is not yet confirmed.

organizer: Varkey Foundation, in partnership with Chegg.org
eligibility_verbatim: Applicants must be at least 16 years old and currently enrolled in an academic institution or training program (traditional and non-traditional/part-time/online formats accepted). Open to students in every kind of school and, subject to local laws, in every country in the world.
turkey_access_reasoning: Official page confirms worldwide eligibility with no citizenship/country restriction, and explicitly includes students in 'every kind of school' (not just university) from age 16+. The 2025 prize drew nominations/applications from 148 countries, evidencing genuine worldwide reach.
international_access_notes: Fully online application/nomination process; no travel required to apply. Ceremony attendance for finalists may involve travel but is not a barrier to applying.
geographic_restrictions: None found; explicitly worldwide 'subject to local laws.'

evidence.raw_excerpt: At least 16 years old... currently enrolled in an academic institution or training program. Part-time and online students are also eligible... $100,000 annual award... from almost 11,000 nominations and applications from 148 countries... Applications and nominations for the 2026 prize will open [later].

notes_uncertainties: Extremely selective in practice (one global winner/year from tens of thousands of nominations), so realistic expected value for an individual student is recognition-tier (Top 50/Top 10 finalist) rather than the headline prize -- product should present this as a long-shot prestige award, not a likely funding source. 2026 cycle deadline not yet published as of this research date.

organizer: Tempus Public Foundation, on behalf of the Hungarian Government (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade)
host_institution: Various Hungarian higher education institutions (approx. 30 partner institutions)
eligibility_verbatim: Applicants apply as nominees of their country's designated 'sending partner' (for Türkiye, coordinated via the relevant Turkish authority per bilateral agreement). Available for bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's, doctoral, and non-degree preparatory programmes. Applicants apply with their high school diploma for bachelor's programmes. A minimum entrance-exam-style score threshold applies (56/100 referenced in the application guide).
turkey_access_reasoning: Türkiye is directly confirmed as a listed sending partner country on the official Stipendium Hungaricum partners page (visible in the country dropdown), and independent sourcing referencing the official 2026/27 Call for Applications describes approx. 900 study programmes in foreign languages available to Turkish applicants through 30 Hungarian institutions. Available fields for Türkiye specifically are governed by the bilateral agreement and not all fields may be open every year -- applicants should check the current country-specific field list before applying.
international_access_notes: Instruction is in foreign languages (typically English) for most Stipendium Hungaricum programmes, not requiring Hungarian; a free preparatory Hungarian language course is offered.
geographic_restrictions: Restricted to citizens of countries with an active bilateral sending-partner agreement with Hungary; Türkiye is confirmed as one such country.
current_cycle_label: 2026/27 intake cycle already closed (deadline 2026-01-15); 2027/28 cycle not yet published as of 2026-08-26
cost_notes: No application fee found; scholarship itself is fully funded (tuition-free plus stipend).
output_type: undergraduate degree from a Hungarian university

evidence.raw_excerpt: 15th January 2026, 2 pm (CET)... Direct application to universities is not permitted; all applications go through the official online system... minimum 56/100 points required... monthly stipend and accommodation contribution.
Türkiye appears in the dropdown menu of sending partner countries on the Stipendium Hungaricum Partners page.

notes_uncertainties: The 2026/27 deadline (2026-01-15) has already passed as of this research date (2026-08-26); recorded deadline as null per the 'unknown is allowed' rule rather than reusing the passed date. Exact list of fields open to Turkish applicants specifically (vs. the full ~900-programme catalogue) was not independently confirmed by us on an official page and should be checked per-cycle by the next owner.

canonical_name: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship — Undergraduate (Embassy Recommendation)
organizer: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology of Japan (MEXT), administered via the Embassy of Japan in Türkiye
host_institution: Various Japanese universities (assigned after a 1-year Japanese language preparatory period)
eligibility_verbatim: Under 25 years of age and have completed 12 years of school education or have completed courses in a school comparable to a Japanese high school. Candidates sit exams in Japanese, English, mathematics, and science (2 of chemistry/physics/biology for science track) administered by the Embassy.
turkey_access_reasoning: Confirmed via an official Turkish government source: the Turkish Higher Education Council (YÖK, uluslararasi.yok.gov.tr) posted an official May 2026 bulletin stating Turkish students can apply for the 2027 MEXT undergraduate/research scholarships, administered by the 'Embassy of Japan in Türkiye,' with preliminary screening by the Embassy and final decision by MEXT Tokyo.
international_access_notes: Application and preliminary exams are conducted in Türkiye at the Japanese Embassy in Ankara; no travel to Japan required to apply. Program includes a mandatory 1-year Japanese language preparatory course before the 4-year (or longer, for medicine/dentistry/pharmacy/vet science) degree.
geographic_restrictions: Country-specific application timeline/quota set by each Japanese embassy; confirmed open to Türkiye via the YÖK bulletin and the Embassy of Japan in Türkiye.
output_type: monthly stipend (¥242,000/month per official figure found for the 2027 track generally)
5-year undergraduate degree (7 years for medicine/dentistry/pharmacy/vet science)

evidence.raw_excerpt: under 25 years of age and have completed 12 years of school education or have completed courses in a school comparable to a Japanese high school... Monthly stipend: ¥242,000 per month... Tuition: Exempted... Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided... 5 years including Japanese language training (7 years for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary science).

2027 Japanese Government Scholarship... The announcement of the scholarship program and the preliminary evaluation process for applicants will be conducted by the Embassy of Japan, while the final admission decision will be made by [MEXT]... For detailed information: Embassy of Japan in Türkiye. Posted by YÖK Department of International Relations, 15 May 2026.

notes_uncertainties: Exact 2027-cycle application window/deadline specific to the Türkiye embassy was not found on an official page we could fetch (the Embassy of Japan in Türkiye's own scholarship sub-page was not successfully reached; application_url therefore points to the general MEXT/Study in Japan page rather than a guessed embassy URL). Next owner should locate and confirm the live Embassy-of-Japan-in-Türkiye application page and exact deadline before marking production-ready. ¥242,000/month figure was labeled for the '2027 intake' generally, not embassy-specific; amounts can vary slightly by cohort.

canonical_name: Three Dot Dash: Global Teen Leaders Program
eligibility_verbatim: Ages 13-19. Must be working on an environmental solution or climate-related initiative, and have launched (or be building) an innovation or organization to create change. Requires a Pre-Application, Main Application, and a Nominator Form (nominator must be an educator, WAFF alumni, coalition partner, WAFF team member, or an unrelated community champion).
turkey_access_reasoning: No citizenship/country restriction found on the official page; program describes a 'global network of changemakers spanning 75+ countries and six continents.' Condition: requires a qualifying nominator (educator, alumni, coalition partner, or community champion who is not a relative/close friend) -- a real access barrier but not a geographic one. Applications for the most recent cycle were closed at time of research.
international_access_notes: Selected Global Teen Leaders attend an in-person one-week summit (most recent cycle: London) -- funded international travel is part of the program, but this also means participation if selected requires travel/visa logistics for a Turkey-based teen.
geographic_restrictions: None explicitly found; described as global (75+ countries, six continents).
current_cycle_label: cycle closed at time of research; next cycle not yet open
output_type: year-long virtual mentorship with an expert

evidence.raw_excerpt: 13–19 years old... working on an environmental solution or climate-related initiative... APPLICATIONS ARE NOW CLOSED... attend a one-week summit in London this fall... join a year of virtual learning with 20+ peers... paired with an expert mentor... WE ARE FAMILY FOUNDATION CURRENTLY HAS NO OPEN APPLICATIONS.

notes_uncertainties: Current cycle's environmental/climate theme framing may be specific to this year's edition (past cycles reportedly covered broader 'basic human needs' themes per third-party summaries, not independently confirmed by us) -- next owner should re-check the theme when applications next open. No evidence found of a past Turkish Global Teen Leader, so real-world Turkey uptake is unconfirmed even though eligibility rules do not exclude Türkiye.

eligibility_verbatim: Young people between the ages of 8 and 16 who have completed (or nearly completed) an environmental project of their own. Applications must be submitted in English.
eligible_grades: Roughly elementary through early high school (grades ~3-10 depending on system)
turkey_access_reasoning: Official page states the program is worldwide: 'Youth from countries around the globe' / 'young people from all around the world' -- no citizenship or country restriction found. Condition: the maximum age of 16 excludes older high schoolers (17-18-year-old juniors/seniors), so this is only useful for a Turkey-based student in the earlier years of high school (or one who completes a project before turning 17), and English-language application is required.
international_access_notes: Fully online application; no travel required.
minimum_activity_duration: Per a secondary source summarizing prior-cycle guidelines (not independently re-confirmed by us on the official page fetched): project should be at least 6 months in duration and either close to completion or completed within the last year.
current_cycle_label: cycle timing unclear at time of research

evidence.raw_excerpt: young people between the ages of 8 and 16... Youth from countries around the globe... Winners receive a cash prize of up to $1,000, a special certificate of achievement, public recognition on our website and in the media, as well as exclusive access to our Eco-Hero Alumni Facebook Group.

notes_uncertainties: Official page fetched did not show a specific current-cycle deadline; a secondary source referenced a 'previous deadline of February 28, 2026' for the 2026 cycle (already passed as of this research date) -- 2027 cycle deadline not confirmed on an official page, recorded as null rather than assumed. Age cap of 16 is a meaningful limitation for the target demographic (many Turkey-based applicants to international universities are 17-18 at application time) -- flagged clearly rather than glossed over.

organizer: Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan), jointly with Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Taiwan)
eligibility_verbatim: Foreign national with at least a secondary school graduation diploma, excellent academic record, good moral character. Undergraduate applicants need a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.5 scale. Ineligible if: R.O.C. (Taiwan) national, already studying in Taiwan, already completed the same degree level in Taiwan, already received 5 total years of Taiwan Scholarship funding, or had a prior scholarship revoked.
turkey_access_reasoning: Confirmed directly on the official Taipei Economic and Cultural Mission in Ankara website (roc-taiwan.org, the Turkish-language site of Taiwan's diplomatic mission to Türkiye) -- 'Taiwan Scholarship 2026 will be open for application' addressed to applicants in Türkiye, with documents to be mailed to the Mission in Ankara and a named contact email. This is Taiwan's de facto embassy-equivalent in Türkiye (Taiwan and Türkiye do not have formal diplomatic relations, hence 'Mission' rather than Embassy), confirming genuine Turkey-based access.
international_access_notes: Application and document submission handled via the Taipei Economic and Cultural Mission in Ankara -- no travel to Taiwan needed to apply.
geographic_restrictions: Open to foreign nationals generally (worldwide), applied for via the applicant's local Taiwan representative office; a Türkiye-specific process is confirmed via the Ankara mission.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle (already closed); 2027 cycle not yet published

evidence.raw_excerpt: Applications open February 1 to March 31, 2026... The MOE will pay up to NTD 40,000 each semester for each recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses... monthly stipend of NTD 15,000 [undergraduate]... maximum four years for bachelor's degrees... Submit three copies of required documents via registered mail to the Taipei Economic and Cultural Mission in Ankara by March 31... Contact: uozdere@mofa.gov.tw.

notes_uncertainties: The 2026 cycle deadline (Feb 1 - Mar 31, 2026) has already passed as of this research date (2026-08-26); recorded deadline as null per the 'unknown is allowed' rule rather than reusing the passed 2026 date. Historical pattern strongly suggests the 2027 cycle will open on a similar Feb-Mar timeline, but this is inference, not a confirmed published date. Taiwan is a less central destination for this product's 'primarily US/UK/Europe' framing, but is a legitimate, well-evidenced, fully-funded government scholarship genuinely accessible to a Türkiye-based student, so it is included.
